# MDRS-104 — a users table, `GET/PATCH /me` and exact e-mail lookup

## What was done

**Schema (migration `0016_users`, generated by drizzle-kit).** `users`:

| column | type | source |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | `uuid` primary key | the token's `sub` |
| `email` | `text`, nullable | token `email` |
| `email_verified` | `boolean`, default false | token `email_verified` (only a real `true` counts) |
| `given_name`, `family_name` | `text`, nullable | token claims |
| `time_zone` | `text`, nullable | `PATCH /me` only (IANA zone, MDRS-110) |
| `locale` | `text`, nullable | token `locale` on first insert; `PATCH /me` after that |
| `created_at`, `last_seen_at` | `timestamptz` | server |

Plus a non-unique index on `lower(email)`. Not unique on purpose: Keycloak can
give an address to a second account before the first account's row has been
refreshed, and a unique constraint would then fail that user's requests.

**Recording the caller.** `UserSyncInterceptor` is a global `APP_INTERCEPTOR`.
Interceptors run after guards, so on every route behind `AuthGuard` it sees
the verified claims; on unauthenticated routes there is no `request.user` and
it does nothing. It awaits the write before the handler, so `GET /me` reads the
row its own request created. `UserSyncService` keeps a per-process cache
(`sub` → claim fingerprint + time, capped at 10 000 entries, oldest evicted):
unchanged claims inside a 3-hour window cost no query. A changed e-mail,
verification flag or name bypasses the cache. The upsert is
`INSERT … ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE … WHERE <something changed> OR
last_seen_at < now() - 3h`, so a cache miss on another instance or after a
restart does not rewrite an unchanged row. A failed write is logged and the
request continues; the cache is not updated, so the next request retries.
A `sub` that is not a UUID is skipped (every user column in tedrisat is `uuid`).

**`GET /me`** — profile plus `roles`: `systemAdmin` (the `SYSTEM_ADMIN` realm
role, via `AuthzService.isSystemAdmin`), `manages` (köşks owned, via the new
`KoskService.findManagedBy`), `teaches` (courses listing the caller in
`course_muderris`, via the new `CourseRepository.findTaughtBy`), `nazirOf`.

**`PATCH /me`** — `timeZone` (`@IsTimeZone`) and `locale` (`@IsLocale`); `null`
clears, an absent field is left alone, any other field is a 400.

**`GET /users?email=`** — exact, case-insensitive match, zero or one result
(`id`, `givenName`, `familyName`, `email`). Callers: `SYSTEM_ADMIN` and anyone
who owns at least one köşk; everyone else gets `403 USER_LOOKUP_FORBIDDEN`. A
value that is not an e-mail address is a 400. The check lives in `UserService`,
not in `@Authz`, because "is a köşk manager anywhere" is not a role on one
resource, which is what the matrix expresses.

**Client.** Spec and typed client regenerated (`pnpm run openapi:tedrisat`):
new `MeApi`, `UsersApi` and seven models. As in MDRS-95, generated files whose
only change was the document-version header were left untouched. The new APIs
are not yet wired into `libs/services`' `api` object — nothing calls them yet.

## What was verified

- `nx affected -t typecheck test build lint module-boundaries --base=11cce33`:
  green for tedrisat, nizam-web, tedris-web, services and their dependencies.
  tedrisat: 27 suites, 438 tests (from the run's `coverage/junit.xml`).
- `test/e2e/user.e2e.spec.ts` (21 tests) runs the real `AuthGuard` against
  minted tokens: first request creates the row; a changed e-mail updates it;
  unchanged claims do not rewrite `last_seen_at`; no row for a 401;
  `GET /me` roles for an admin, a köşk manager, a müderris and a talebe;
  `PATCH /me` set / clear / reject; the token's `locale` does not overwrite a
  user-set one; `GET /users` 403 for a talebe and for a müderris without a
  köşk, 200 with one result (also case-insensitive) or zero (unknown address,
  prefix) for a köşk manager, 200 for an admin, 400 for a non-address.
- `test/unit/user/user-sync.spec.ts` (8 tests): cache window, expiry, change
  detection, retry after a failed write, claim normalisation.
- `node tools/ci/assert-openapi-spec-fresh.mjs`: green.

## What was not verified

- Against the real realm: that production tokens carry `email`,
  `email_verified`, `given_name`, `family_name` and `locale` (Keycloak's
  default `profile`/`email` scopes do; not checked on auth.medaris.app).
- Behaviour under load, and the cache across several instances.

## Follow-up

- **Nazır.** tedrisat has no medrese or medrese→nazır table, so `nazirOf` is
  always `[]` and nazırs cannot yet use `GET /users`. Both switch on when that
  table lands (MDRS-107); the two places are marked in `UserService`.
- **Köşk creation is still open.** `POST /kosks` carries no `@Authz`, so any
  authenticated user can create a köşk today and thereby pass the
  `GET /users` permission check. The lookup stays exact-match (an e-mail →
  name oracle, not a list), but the "managers only" boundary only holds once
  MDRS-107 restricts köşk creation.
- **Privacy notice (MDRS-102).** The acceptance criterion "the privacy notice
  lists what this table stores" is not met here: the notice does not exist in
  the repository yet. The table above is the list it needs.
- `kosks.owner_id` and `course_muderris.user_id` have no index of their own;
  `GET /me` and the lookup's permission check filter on them. Fine at today's
  size; add indexes if they show up in a profile.
